title: Private player journals + GM journal, ingested as growing context
summary: Each PC gets a Foundry journal only they can see, for their own notes; the GM gets one too, populated via a timestamped text field in a GM management tool. After a session, the difference since last checked gets ingested as additional context for writing future episodes.
description:
Each player character gets a private JournalEntry visible only to that player, for recording their own in-character or out-of-character thoughts as the campaign goes. A parallel GM journal exists, populated by a timestamped text field inside whatever GM-facing management tool gets built — the GM's own version of the same idea.

The point: after a session, the *difference* in these journals since they were last checked gets ingested as additional context for writing the next episode. This is a direct, concrete use case for the harvest mechanism already designed in design/foundry-module-design.md §4 (promotable content, GM-pulled, not automatic) — private journal content is exactly the kind of thing that should never be pushed/overwritten and should only ever move Foundry-to-repo. Combined with chat-log-knowledge-base, the intent is a complete picture of a session — including when players go somewhere the plan never anticipated, and the GM's own improvised notes about how they handled it — so future episodes can actually respond to what happened rather than what was planned.
sourceContext: User planning message on dialogue/journal/campaign-management systems, prior to the ideas/ system existing — originally captured as prose in design/campaign-arc.md's 'Foundry module: new concept threads' section, migrated here on audit.
